title: Module quiz: Errors, retries and timeouts

blocks.text: Questions on what this page has just taught. Choose one answer for each.

questions.stem: A job's calls sometimes fail with a lost network link, and sometimes with a 409 because two workers touched the same resource. Which handling fits the page?

options.text: Repeat both at once with no delay, since every failure is temporary and clears by itself
options.says: Ruled out because a 409 is retried only "once the conflict is resolved".

options.text: Repeat the first kind, and the second only after the clash is resolved
options.says: The page's table lists "A lost or timed-out connection (no status)" and "408, 409 (once the conflict is resolved)" under "Retry".

options.text: Repeat neither, since a status error is always the fault of the request that was sent
options.says: Ruled out because a lost link is retried: "A lost or timed-out connection (no status)" is the first row.

options.text: Repeat only the second, since the first has no status that the code could read
options.says: Ruled out because the SDKs retry "because of a network connectivity problem" as well.

questions.stem: A user-facing summary call has a budget of 2,000 ms. Its client allows three attempts with a 1,000 ms timeout and waits 500 ms, then 1,000 ms, between them. What is the worst case for the caller?

options.text: About four and a half seconds, which is more than twice the target
options.says: The page's formula is "attempts x timeout + sum of the waits between attempts": three seconds of attempts and one and a half seconds of waits make four and a half.

options.text: One second, because the timeout bounds the whole call from start to finish
options.says: Ruled out because "the time a caller may wait is not the timeout".

options.text: About two seconds, because the waits between the attempts are not counted
options.says: Ruled out because the formula adds "the waits between attempts".

options.text: Thirty seconds, because the default timeout still applies to every attempt
options.says: Ruled out because the page has you "choose a per-attempt timeout and an attempt count that fit under it", and a one-second timeout replaces the ten-minute default.

origin.section: The worst case is a product

questions.stem: Users behind a corporate proxy report that streamed answers arrive in one lump and, now and then, as an HTML page. Which origin does the page point to first?

options.text: The network path, where a device rewrites or buffers the traffic
options.says: The page's table lists "works locally, fails behind the proxy" under the path, with the checks "Is the body still JSON? Is the stream buffered?".

options.text: Their credential, which the proxy has stripped from the calls
options.says: Ruled out because a credential fault is a "401 or 403 from one environment only", and a stripped key would not give an HTML page with partial streaming.

options.text: Capacity, because the provider could not take every request
options.says: Ruled out because capacity means "the request was fine and the service could not take it now", with a 429 or 529 status.

options.text: The output limit, because the replies are cut before the end
options.says: Ruled out because a cut reply is "replies cut mid-sentence, status 200" and does not come as HTML.

questions.stem: Errors with status 529 appear in bursts each time a marketing campaign multiplies the job's traffic. What does the page's table suggest?

options.text: Raise the output limit, since the replies are probably being cut before the end
options.says: Ruled out because a cut reply is "Replies cut mid-sentence, status 200", not a 529.

options.text: Rotate the key, since the credential is the likely origin of such errors
options.says: Ruled out because the credential row is about "Which key does that environment load?", and a 529 is no credential fault.

options.text: Back off, and bring the load up in gradual steps
options.says: The table lists "529 in bursts" with the check "Is your traffic ramping fast?" and the cure "Back off; ramp up gradually".

options.text: Fix the proxy, since the network path is the likely origin of such errors
options.says: Ruled out because the path row is "Is the body still JSON? Is the stream buffered?", and a 529 carries a JSON body.
